title: A Mindful Way to Use Cannabis | House of Zen
h1: A Mindful Way to Use Cannabis
description: A slow way to use cannabis, built on intention and attention: choosing the time, setting the room, taking a small amount and noticing, with no promises.
excerpt: An ordinary thing done with care is worth an hour of anyone’s time. This is how we would set about it, the way you might set about making tea.
pull: A tea ceremony promises nothing and asks only that you pay attention to the next small thing.

blocks.html: Balance, education and intention are words we use a lot at House of Zen. The last of those is the easiest to practice. It only means deciding what you are doing before you do it.

A tea ceremony is a good picture of this. Water is heated, a bowl is wiped, the tea is whisked and passed along. The tea itself is ordinary. A tea ceremony promises nothing and asks only that you pay attention to the next small thing.

We think cannabis can be approached the same way by anyone who already enjoys it. Not to arrive anywhere in particular. Simply because an ordinary thing done with care is a better way to spend an hour than the same thing done in a hurry.
Start with a plain question: do I want this today? Some days the honest answer is no, and that counts as practice too.

If the answer is yes, choose a time when nobody needs you and you have nowhere to drive. An empty evening or a slow weekend morning will do. Decide roughly how much you will have while your head is clear, and then keep to it.

Clear a table. Put the phone in another room. Open a window or turn on a lamp you like, whichever suits the hour, and pour a glass of water or make a pot of tea before you sit down. Lay out what you need in the order you will use it, as a cook does.
Think, too, about who shares the air. If anyone else is at home, especially children, this happens somewhere else or it waits for another day.

items: Smell the flower before you do anything else. If you are curious what you are smelling, read about terpenes.
Break it up or grind it by hand, without rushing. If you are using a pre-roll, look it over first, then light it evenly.
Take one small draw and set everything down. You do not have to finish a pre-roll: it can be put out and kept for another day.
Wait at least ten minutes. Notice the taste, your breathing, the room, whatever happens to be there. Nothing in particular is supposed to happen.
Only then decide whether you want any more. “No” is a fine place to end.

blocks.html: Put things away and rinse the glass. Clearing up belongs to the ritual as much as the beginning does. A tea ceremony, after all, ends with the host cleaning the bowl.
Some people keep a small notebook: what they used, how much, what they noticed. Keep it as a record rather than a scorecard, because there is no right result here.
This is a way of paying attention, not a health practice. We make no promises about how cannabis will make you feel, and questions about your health belong with your doctor.
If you would like to talk through what to choose for a slow session like this, come and see us. Our shop is a judgment-free place, and nobody here is in a hurry.

faq.q: Do I need to meditate or know anything about tea?
faq.a_html: No. The tea ceremony is only a picture of the idea. All you need is a little time, a clear table and your attention.
Less than you think. If you are new to cannabis, our guide for beginners is a better place to start than this one.

faq.q: Can I do this with an edible?
faq.a_html: You can, though the timing changes. An edible can take two hours or more to arrive, so the waiting is longer, and starting low matters more.
